why: `eval` runs its code where it is, in the workspace around it, once its argument is evaluated: after the code before it and before the code after it (MATLAB doc 'eval'), and a script runs in its caller's workspace, so what it assigns is a variable there once it has run (MATLAB doc 'Scripts vs. Functions'; the project's script-workspace rule, src/resolution/matlab-script-workspace.ts: a bare name's failed call that a script run strictly before it makes is kept dormant). Code a variable holds is no text written where `eval` is, and still runs there: in `runner.m` the script it runs makes `XV` before `XV(2)` reads it (dormant), in `runner3.m` `XV(2)` is read before the statement runs it (failed), and the two runs in `runner4.m`'s text are two calls of their own (found by the step 14 second review: code given so was read after every call on its line).
